## Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900

**My pick: BLUETTI AC200L — $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF.**

Based on your nine supplied pages, it's the strongest overall choice for RV use because it combines a true 2kWh LiFePO4 battery, a built-in 30A RV outlet (TT-30), solid output, and good solar charging.

<AsyncImageGroup query={["BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view TT-30 RV outlet","Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 portable power station product","Renogy PowerStation 2000 portable power station product"]} aspectRatio="4:3" layout="bento"/>

## Top 3 compared

| Feature | **BLUETTI AC200L** | Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | Renogy PowerStation 2000 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Capacity | 2,048Wh | 2,048Wh | 2,048Wh |
| AC output | 2,400W | 2,400W | 2,400W |
| RV outlet (TT-30) | Yes | Yes (20A) | Yes |
| Solar input | 1,200W | 800W | 1,200W |
| Weight | 62.4 lb | **41.7 lb** | 51.8 lb |
| Price | **$854.05 with coupon** | $899.99 | $849 |

Source: [DealElectric's direct comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

## Why I'd choose the BLUETTI AC200L

- **RV-ready:** Plug your RV's 30A shore-power cord directly into the built-in TT-30 outlet.
- **Good capacity and output:** 2,048Wh battery and 2,400W AC inverter.
- **Strong solar capability:** Up to 1,200W solar input, matching Renogy.
- **Fits your budget:** The reported 5% coupon brings it down to $854.05.
- **Good value:** The GearRanking RV roundup also identifies it as a competitive option in the 2kWh class, while Renogy and other alternatives are worth considering.

### Buy link
[BLUETTI AC200L — listed deal and purchase link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

## Important RV limitation

A built-in 30A outlet **does not mean you get 30A of power.**

The AC200L's 2,400W inverter delivers roughly 20A at 120V. It's suitable for:

- RV refrigerator
- Lights and fans
- Water pump
- Coffee maker
- Electronics and chargers

But don't expect it to run your rooftop air conditioner reliably, especially during compressor startup. Running a microwave and electric kettle simultaneously could also exceed its output.

Also, if your RV's onboard converter is charging its house battery, it can consume up to approximately 800W. Turn the converter off once the battery is charged to conserve power. For a two-way refrigerator, propane mode is preferable to AC mode when off-grid.

Source: [DealElectric — What a 30A RV plug really gets](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

## When I'd choose another model

  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 — best for portability**

      At 41.7 lb, it's nearly 21 lb lighter than the BLUETTI. Same 2,048Wh capacity and 2,400W output, with a TT-30 outlet. I'd choose it if moving the unit frequently is important.

      [Anker details and pricing](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)
    </box>
  </row>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Renogy PowerStation 2000 2048Wh portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Renogy PowerStation 2000 — best alternative for value**

      At $849, it offers the same 2,048Wh and 2,400W, TT-30, and 1,200W solar input. A strong alternative if you prefer Renogy's ecosystem.

      [Renogy official product page](https://www.renogy.com/collections/all-products/products/power-station-2000)
    </box>
  </row>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO — best budget pick**

      GearRanking lists it at $676.16 for 2,048Wh and 2,400W, with an RV outlet. Excellent value if saving money is your main priority.

      [GearRanking RV comparison](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

---

## Bottom line

I'd buy the **BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05** if the coupon is still working. For frequent lifting in and out of your RV, I'd seriously consider the **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2** instead, because its 41.7 lb weight is a major practical advantage.

One caveat: these prices are from the pages you provided, checked October 30–31, 2026, and may change.

judge.why: The answer recommends our BLUETTI AC200L using dealectric.com figures, but it never covers weekend runtime (1.2-1.5 kWh/day, about 1.5 days, 2-3 days with solar) or recharge options like an alternator charger or campground outlet.
judge.concern: How long a 2 kWh station lasts on an RV weekend: about 1.2-1.5 kWh a day (fridge, furnace blower, lights), so about a day and a half on its own and two to three days with 200-400 W of solar, and how to recharge it (solar, an alternator charger, a campground outlet).
